name: Romam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Long Olsen, Emily. 2015. [Preliminary phonological research on Romam (North Bahnaric; Kon Tum, Vietnam); title not given]. Unpublished manuscript, The Graduate Center, City University of New York. Known only from in-text citations in Olsen, Emily Long. 2018. The sound patterns of Kachok in the context of Bahnaric and North-Bahnaric studies. PhD dissertation, The Graduate Center, CUNY, pp. 62, 84, 178-179 (Romam register/pitch statements at printed pp. 101-102 and 178-179); the same dissertation separately cites 'Long Olsen 2012, unpublished manuscript' (Romam field data, pp. 13, 59) - request both from the author together.
tone_statements.quote: While Kachok uses breathiness as a contrastive feature, Romam appears (from preliminary research, Long Olsen 2015, unpublished manuscript) to have a register contrast in which its two phonological registers are marked by a wider range of phonetic features including pitch. While these comparisons and conclusions are only preliminary and will require a more complete study of Romam in order to investigate them fully, one possible hypothesis is that Romam has been influenced by Vietnamese in developing contrastive pitch, while the breathiness in Kachok evolved under the influence of other local Bahnaric languages.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 178-179, section 5.2 'Phonology in context of local languages and subfamilies' (body header at that page; 5.3 'Open questions' follows on p. 179). Additional, more specific statement at pp. 101-102 ('pitch is an apparent marker of the tense register.. in some iterations of minimal pairs, the primary phonetic correlate is pitch'). Real

sources.citation: Olsen, Emily L. 2018. The sound patterns of Kachok in the context of Bahnaric and North-Bahnaric studies. PhD dissertation, CUNY Graduate Center.
sources.note: Full phonology with a prosodic model of the sesquisyllable for the sister variety Kachok (kaco1236, Ratanakiri); would give the closest explicit stress statement for the Lamamic pair and may discuss Romam. Identity caveat: not roma1331.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2015. Austroasiatic dataset for phylogenetic analysis: 2015 version. Mon-Khmer Studies 44: lxviii-ccclvii.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist only; 'Ramam rmx 86.5 Sidwell ms. Fieldnotes.' (p. lxxiv) is the source line. IPA forms (e.g. kətɔh, pətuk, həmɯl, təhãːj) show unstressed schwa presyllables but no stress marking or prose on stress.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii.
sources.note: p. xxxv: 'Romam is only briefly mentioned in the Ethnologue, but is not discussed in any known English language sources.' p. xxxvii, family-level only: 'Phonological words in Bahnaric may be mono- or disyllabic, with the latter generally treated as sesquisyllablic (iambic stress).' No Romam-specific data; lists Romam rmx as EGIDS 6a (p. lxii).

sources.citation: Võ Đức Tám. [c. 2013-2014, undated]. Âm tiết trong tiếng Rơ-măm [Syllable in Rơ-măm language]. 8 pp. MA-programme paper, Lớp Cao học ngôn ngữ K2012, Khoa Ngữ Văn, Trường Đại học Khoa học, Đại học Huế. Vietnamese with English summary.
sources.note: Nothing explicit: no occurrence of 'trọng âm' (stress) or 'nhấn'. Describes a sesquisyllabic word: monosyllable = major syllable (ÂTC); polysyllable = minor syllable/presyllable (ÂTP, CV(C) or nasal N) + major syllable, presyllable always first; major syllable is the 'nucleus' (hạt nhân), presyllable vowel is a neutral schwa that often deletes in connected speech (pp. 2-6). Classifies Rơ-măm as 'cận âm tiết tính' (sesquisyllabic) per Nguyễn Quang Hồng (p. 6). Author states no prior structural description of Rơ-măm exists (p. 1).

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., Kenneth Gregerson & Paul Sidwell. 2011. The North Bahnaric clade: a computational approach. In Sidwell & Srichampa (eds.), Austroasiatic Studies: papers from ICAAL4 (Mon-Khmer Studies Special Issue No. 3), 23-37. Dallas/Canberra/Salaya.
sources.note: Comparative/lexicostatistical paper that discusses the Kaco'/Ramam identity confusion and uses Ramam wordlist data; would settle which fieldnotes underlie the Sidwell 2015 Ramam list. Unlikely to state stress.
